entries.meaning: From Biblical Hebrew יַעֲקֹב (yaʿăqōḇ, literally “he will/shall heel”).
entries.note: A male given name from Hebrew, variant of Jacob.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Japanese やえこ (Yaeko).
entries.note: A female given name from Japanese.

entries.meaning: Rendering of the modern Israeli Hebrew יעל.
entries.note: A female given name from Hebrew.

entries.meaning: From Spanish Yago, from Latin Iācōbus (“James”), from Ancient Greek Ἰάκωβος (Iákōbos), from Hebrew יַעֲקֹב (ya‘ăqṓḇ, “Jacob”, literally “he will/shall heel”), from עָקֵב (‘āqḗḇ, “heel”) and the Biblical account of the patriarch Jacob's birth in Genesis 25:26. Doublet of Iago, Jago, James, Jacob, and Jacques.
entries.note: A male given name from Spanish.

entries.meaning: From Arabic يَحْيَى (yaḥyā), equivalent to John in the Qur'an.
entries.note: A male given name from Arabic.

entries.meaning: Transliteration of Hebrew יַאִיר, meaning "he will light up".
entries.note: A male given name from Hebrew.

entries.meaning: From the Hebrew masculine form "Ya'akov" or "Yakov" which originally refers to the Biblical character, Jacob.
entries.note: A female given name from Hebrew.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Japanese やま (Yama).
entries.note: A female given name from Japanese.

entries.meaning: From Japanese 大和 (Yamato), itself of uncertain derivation, but likely related to 山 (yama, “mountains”). See Proto-Japonic *yamatə.
entries.note: A male given name from Japanese.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Sanskrit यामिका (yāmikā, “night”).
entries.note: A female given name from Sanskrit used in India.

entries.meaning: From Spanish, derived from Arabic جَمِيلَة (jamīla, “Jamila”, literally “beautiful”).
entries.note: A female given name from Spanish.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Sanskrit यामिनी (yāminī, “night”).
entries.note: A female given name from Sanskrit used in India.

entries.meaning: Cognate to English Jane, ultimately from Hebrew, feminine form of Ioannes ( =John).
entries.note: A female given name from the Slavic languages. A romanization of the Bulgarian or Russian or Ukrainian name Я́на (Jána).

entries.meaning: From French Yannick, from Breton Yannig.
entries.note: A male given name from French.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Arabic يَعْقُوب (yaʕqūb).
entries.note: A male given name, Yaqub, Yakub, and Yacoub, from Arabic

entries.meaning: From Hebrew יַרְדֵּן (yardén, “Jordan”). Doublet of Jordan.
entries.note: A unisex given name from Hebrew.

entries.meaning: Transliteration of Russian and Ukrainian Яросла́в (Jarosláv).

entries.meaning: Transliteration of Russian and Ukrainian Яросла́ва (Jarosláva).

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Sanskrit यश (yaśa, “fame, glory”).

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Russian Я́ша (Jáša) or borrowed from Ukrainian Я́ша (Jáša).
entries.note: A diminutive Яша of the Russian/Ukrainian male given name Яков (Jákov)/Яків (Jákiv), equivalent to English Jake

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Sanskrit यशोदा (yaśodā).

entries.note: A male given name from Japanese.

entries.meaning: From Sanskrit यति (yati, “striver, sage”), synonymous to a spiritual person, yogi or monk. Derives from य (ya) and -ति (-ti).
entries.note: A male given name from India, of Indian usage.

entries.meaning: "Yatish" means "master of all saints" according to Hindu books.
entries.note: A male given name from India.

entries.meaning: The male name is ultimately from Arabic يَحْيَى (yaḥyā); likely through a West African language.

entries.meaning: Transliteration of Arabic يازن.

entries.meaning: From 𐭩𐭦𐭣𐭪𐭫𐭲𐭩 (yzdklty) / Middle Persian 𐭩𐭦𐭣𐭪𐭥𐭲𐭩 (Yazdegerd, Yazdgird, literally “made by God”), from 𐭩𐭦𐭣 (Yazd) + 𐭪𐭥𐭲𐭩 (-gird, -kirt).
entries.note: A transliteration of the Middle Persian male given name 𐭩𐭦𐭣𐭪𐭫𐭲𐭩 (yzdklty) or 𐭩𐭦𐭣𐭪𐭥𐭲𐭩 (Yazdegerd, Yazdgird), notably borne by several Sassanid kings.

entries.meaning: Variant of Yardley.
entries.note: A unisex given name transferred from the surname, of rare usage.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Telugu ఏడుకొండలు (ēḍukoṇḍalu, “seven hills (of Tirumala); alternative name for Venkateswara”).
entries.note: A male given name used among Telugu people.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Russian Ефре́м (Jefrém). Doublet of Ephraim.
entries.note: A transliteration of the Russian male given name Ефре́м (Jefrém).

entries.meaning: From Hebrew יהונתן.

entries.meaning: Transliteration of Hebrew יְהוּדָה (yehudá). Doublet of Judah and Judas.

entries.meaning: From Hebrew יְהוּדִי (yehudí, “Jew”). Related to Judah. An endonym for and doublet of Jew.

entries.meaning: Transliteration of Hebrew יְהוּדִית (y'hudít, “Judith”). Doublet of Judith.
entries.note: A female given name from Hebrew.

entries.meaning: From Bulgarian, Macedonian, and Russian Еле́на (Jeléna), from Latin Helena, from Ancient Greek Ἑλένη (Helénē). Doublet of Helena.
entries.note: A transliteration of the Bulgarian, Macedonian, or Russian female given name Еле́на (Eléna), equivalent to Helen.

entries.meaning: From Russian Елизаве́та (Jelizavéta). Doublet of Elizabeth.
entries.note: A transliteration of the Russian female given name Елизаве́та (Jelizavéta), equivalent to Elizabeth.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Korean 영 (yeong).

entries.meaning: From Russian Ереме́й (Jereméj). Doublet of Jeremy.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Russian Евге́ний (Jevgénij), from Ancient Greek Εὐγένιος (Eugénios). Doublet of Eugene and Eugenius.

entries.meaning: From Spanish Yolanda, the form of a medieval royal name of obscure, probably Germanic, origin. It has been identified with Latin Violante and with Ancient Greek ἴον (íon, “violet”) + ἄνθος (ánthos, “flower”). Doublet of Yolande.

entries.meaning: * As an English, Scottish, and northern Irish surname, from the adjective young, used to distinguish a younger brother or son. This sense is comparable to the surnames le Yunge, German Jong and Junk, Dutch Jong and de Jongh, French Lejeune and LaJeunesse, assimilated from Dion and Guyon. * As a Chinese surname, from the following: ** Cantonese 楊 /杨 (joeng⁴). Doublet of Yeung. ** Hokkien 楊 /杨 (iông / iâng).
entries.note: A surname. A British distinguishing surname transferred from the nickname for the younger of two people having the same given name.

entries.meaning: * (female given name): From the propensity of female Chinese given names to reduplicate a syllable, resulting in a reduplicated syllable in the coining of an English given name not originating as a Chinese name.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from French Yvette. The politics sense is a reference to the name of a docile young girl in a school textbook, and was popularized by separatist politician Lise Payette (1931–2018).
entries.note: A female given name from French borrowed from French in the nineteenth century.
entries.origin: French borrowed from French in the nineteenth century

entries.meaning: From the French feminine form of Yvon, variant of Yves, from a Germanic root for "yew" (see Old English iw). It might have originally been used of an archer, since yew wood was used to make bows.
entries.note: A female given name from French borrowed from France, in regular use since the twentieth century.
